what_is_learned: the PDE coefficients (alpha) and the missing source q(x)
notes: Canonical rod of heat1d: alpha = 0.1, 128 points, FTCS to t_f = 0.05, 26 snapshots per trajectory; 20 training profiles (seed 1), 10 test profiles (seed 3); no validation split (the single threshold is chosen on the fit-error plateau). Case A: np.gradient derivatives, library ['1', 'T', 'T_x', 'T_xx', 'T_xxx', 'T^2', 'T T_x'], STLSQ lambda = 0.0501; recovered T_t = 0.1009 T_xx with no spurious term; the recovered PDE is marched by the same FTCS scheme on the test profiles. Case B: reference with q(x) = 20 sin(2 pi x); residual T_t - 0.1 T_xx regressed on ['1', 'sin(pi x)', 'sin(2pi x)', 'sin(3pi x)', 'sin(4pi x)', 'x', 'x^2'] with lambda = 0.0316; recovered 20.0155 sin(2 pi x), no spurious term; marching alpha = 0.1 plus the discovered source gives test rel L2 mean 6.59e-04 (source omitted: median 0.65). Noise: 1 % Gaussian noise on T, finite differences, same rule: alpha = 0.0290, spurious {} (the form survives, the coefficient is attenuated by SNR^2/(1+SNR^2) = 0.287); weak form (space-time bumps, 1440 rows): alpha = 0.1004, no spurious term. Costs: one FTCS solve of the recovered equation, measured; train_time_s is the case-A regression (library + threshold sweep + fit).
